text: Is there an Executive (or executive position) who champions data and analytics or innovation? (This might include a Chief Data Officer, Chief Analytics Officer, or BICC Executive Sponsor or similar titles).
Do your Executives get the data and analytic results that they need?
How effectively is data and analytics used to support business processes?

Does your organisation have an "Analytics as a Service" function (either internally or contracted externally) where analytics skills (ranging from report developers through to data scientists) are available on call to assist in delivering business outcomes?
Business Category - Strategy

How do senior executives communicate the vision and goals? Are their direct reports and their organizations aware of the enterprise vision and goals?  Are their direct reports and their organizations aware of areas specific vision and goals and how those support the enterprise?
If you have multiple business units, do they share a common vision for data and analytics?
Is there a primary driver in your industry that is moving you toward a specific vision or capability?
Are there regulatory/compliance needs driving your organization’s priorities?
What are the business’s biggest challenges in getting the information they need from IT?
What are IT’s biggest challenges in providing the data and the tools needed by the business?
What are your strategic business initiatives for the next 12-18 months? What would the Executives say are the most pressing issues or challenges with analytics or data?
What needs or questions does your business have that is currently not able to be addressed with your existing analytics and data warehouse environment?
Business Category - Roadmap
Who develops the overall data and analytics strategy?  Is there an analytic roadmap? If so, who is responsible for executing and updating the roadmap?
How are executives kept informed of priority projects and their status?

How involved are senior executives involved in the review and resolution of cross-functional issues? How are they involved in the prioritization and budgeting of projects? Is there an executive champion assigned to critical projects or programs?
Business Category - Investment/Funding
How are data and analytic needs reviewed, prioritized and budgeted?
Is an approved business case required for analytics projects?

Describe the process for identifying and prioritizing projects.  Describe the criteria used when prioritizing (i.e. Complexity, Costs, Projected Benefits, Prerequisite Needs, Resource Needs, etc.). How far out does the planning go?
Do all projects fall into this process, or are there different processes based on the project’s estimated cost, resource needs, or business function?
How are potential projects estimated or qualified in preparation for the prioritization or funding process?
For those projects that do not qualify for prioritization and funding process, how are resources allocated and tracked? How does the business fund analytic discovery?

What is your baseline for projecting data and analytic funding and resource demand? Do you start out with an annual budget that is driven by last year's budget (or example, plus or minus 5%)?  What is included in the funding of data and analytic initiatives (i.e. architecture, technology, business and IT resources, contractors, etc.)?
Who is the final decision maker for funding and prioritization?   Is there an executive level position that provides input for data and analytic needs and priorities to the final decision maker?
Where in your organisation do Data Scientists sit?  Are they in departmental / line of business roles, or in IT, or in a central organisational structure?

IIs there a pool of IT or analytic development resources shared across the business units? Are there different IT or analytic teams for applications and support?  (For example, are dataa & analytic teams organized to support specific tools or enterprise applications, like SAP?).  What about other cross functional teams, such as a BICC or a Data Management or Data Governance team?
How are corporate projects charged back to the business units?  Do you have charge-back mechanism for CPU usage, I/O, or data storage?
Are business cases required to allocate funded?  Are business cases initiated by the business or IT?  What criteria are required for a business case to be approved?
How do you know when it is time to change your solutions or divest of the solutions you have? How do you balance investing and divesting? How is this planned for in your budget?
Who has the CAPEX and resource budget for IT? Who is the decision maker on data and analytic investment?
Are analytics, IT, or business oriented projects separately or independently funded?
Do you have a long term roadmap that you follow that incorporates the major initiatives over the next few years?  If so, how is that managed?
How are the milestones between different projects and initiatives coordinated?
Business Category - Return on Investment
How does the organisation track value delivered from project investments?
How are the ROI numbers in a business justification (e.g. Business Case)  estimated and vetted?
How does the organization monitor and measure the effectiveness (business value) of data and analytics to a business process?

Does each business case contain a measurement plan, which includes determining baseline metrics against which improvements can be projected (and presumably measured)?  How do you know if or when business case projections are achieved?  Is this something that is regularly measured after a project is implemented?

Describe the process of tracking and reporting on actual results. Are baseline metrics established consistent with the business case? Does the ROI analysis include projections of investment costs? Does the ROI analysis include projections of ongoing operating costs such as additional IT maintenance feed, new headcount, etc.?
Do projects consider business and IT costs, needs and priorities?  Which ones get higher exposure/priority?
Are business cases for IT or other operational investments required?

Who is accountable for achievement of ROI goals? What corrective actions are taken if results fall short of projected goals?  Who is responsible for initiating and implementing the corrective actions?
Are metrics common across projects, or specific to a single project? How are users educated about ROI, the metrics, and the process?
When and how is the business case process initiated?  What does the business case consider?
Information Category
Information Category - Summary
Do the business users have access to the data they need to complete their reporting and analysis?
Have you considered the impact of “big data” on your data integration; e.g., are you able to link social media data to your Customer or Product master?
How effective are the security and privacy management policies and processes of your organisation?
How often is data updated?  Are there certain data only available or updated daily or weekly?
Is the data in the analytics ecosystem of sufficient quality to meet most business analytics needs?

How much historical data is immediately available (not archived) for online analysis?  Does the amount of online historical data support analysis requirements such as seasonal, current versus prior period, and period + 1 (13, 25, or 37 month) for trend identification?
Information Category - Data Strategy
Does your organisation have a defined information or data strategy.  Is that strategy capable of dealing with big data as well as traditional data sources?
Do you operate with an underlying principle that data is a corporate asset?  How is this manifested within the organization?
Information Category - Data Roadmap
Do you have a planned sequence to load new sources of data?  Is this sequence well known and agreed by all parties?
Information Category - Data Architecture

Is there an information architecture and corresponding data model(s) that guides where each different type of data should be stored across a range of information and analytics platforms (e.g. IDW, Data Lake, Data Labs etc.)?  Are there data model(s) that allows for integration across analytics platforms?
Can data and analytics users easily find out where data is stored and how it is structured?
Is data stored for analytics in a logically integrated manner, even if spread across multiple platforms?
Is relational data stored in an integrated data model of some type?  What type?
Is non-relational multi-structured data stored in an organised, formatted, logical manner or stored in source format for later integration?
Can anyone load data into any analytic ecosystem, or only into data lab areas?  If anyone can load data anywhere, how is metadata captured and architectural control exerted?
Information Category - Master and Reference Data Mgmt
How is reference and master data managed?  Is this centralised and shared, or maintained by individual systems
How do you define reference and master data within your major transactional applications?  Within your data warehouse, data marts, or data lakes?
What processes are in place to ensure reference data is consistent and that you have visibility to the changes made to various code values? Is this a manual or automated process?
How would you describe the state of master data at your company?  How are master data updates communicated and managed across different functions?
Are your existing data governance policies adequately addressing the naming standards necessary for successful master data management?
Do you have data owners identified for your master data domains?
Have you considered the impact of “big data” on your master data; e.g., are you able to link social media data to your Customer or Product master?
Do you have enterprise business process workflows for each line of business involved in the data governance framework to maintain and approve master data?
Are the master data requirements for all major lines of business known? Are these master data items held in any centralized logical data model or repository?
Do you have a mechanism and rules in place to detect bad, inaccurate, or duplicate data? To what degree does your organization profile its master data?
Is there a set of MDM SLAs agreed on between the business and IT?
Does master data at your company undergo a structured and automated process to be corrected, cleansed, and approved?
Does the data warehouse act as a publisher for master data? In other words, is there bidirectional flow of master data between the operational systems and the data warehouse?
Do you store and track historical changes to your master data?
Do you have insight into the hierarchies and relationships between master data records?
Do you produce data quality metrics on your master data? How frequently are those metrics refreshed and reviewed by the governance committee?
Are the business rules related to your master data documented in the DW metadata repository?
How are changes in master data elements communicated and synchronized across the enterprise?
How does your organization ensure that different systems use data in the same manner and get the same results?
Information Category - MetaData Mgmt

Is Metadata captured along with the data?  Is this business Metadata, operational or technical metadata?  What about data quality metadata? Is metadata specific to a data warehouse or to an analytics environment managed as part of a centralized solution, or do components of metadata exist across multiple platforms?
Are data fields consistently defined across the organization?
Are you able to meet your regulatory requirements for data lineage, etc.?  Describe the challenges and barriers associated with doing so.
Describe the tools, processes, and techniques used to capture metadata information.   How is metadata defined and accessed across the systems?
Who owns and manages metadata?  How do owners communicate changes or challenges?
What are you SMART goals, metrics, and KPI’s associated with metadata management?
How frequently is the metadata content refreshed?  What governance process is followed to standardize and harmonize metadata?
What is the governance process followed to add new metadata sources?  Is it based on business value or usage? Is it compliance driven?
Is there a single, standard tool and methodology for accessing the metadata?  Describe.
How is metadata being used in the enterprise?  Examples could include data lineage, standardizing transformations, impact analysis, or audit and traceability.
Do data stewards or other data governance organizations establish and communicate metadata standards across the organization?
How do end users access definitions, transformation rules, and metric formulas?
Is Metadata seen as a valuable asset or a constraint?
What standards are being used while retrieving, transforming, and storing metadata?
Is there training available for end users and metadata developers?
Information Category - Data Organization
Does your organisation make use of different data states and concepts, such as Data Lake, Data Warehouse, Master Data, Data Projection and Metadata across a variety of architectures and technologies?
Does each data concept have a defined level of data governance?
Does each data concept have a defined level of data integration?
Does each data concept have a defined level of data quality?
How are data states organised across the different data concepts?
Does your organisation have a data lake? What is its main purpose?
Does your organisation have a data warehouse? Is it integrated?
Are the data lake and data warehouse integrated in any way. For example, the data lake may provide source data to the data warehouse for later integration.
Information Category - Data Centricity
Do your data assets require a detailed level of definition to allow you to exploit the data asset?
Do you data assets require a detailed level of defintion to provide value to the organisation?
Information Category - Data Tiers
Do you know what state of data you need to answer your business questions or perform the required analytics (e.g. source data, integrated data, summarised, etc)?
What different levels of refinement does your data pass through?
What level of sharing and reuseability is achieved with your data assets?
Information Category - Data Usage Zones
Does  your organisation have a Discovery/Exploration data zone that allows you to explore the value of data without strict controls?
Does your organisation have a process that allows new valuable data to be published into the operational are once the value of the data is proven?
Information Category - Data Security and Privacy
Does the company have a formal, published data security and privacy policy describing why customer data is collected, what the information is used for, who has access, and when it is deleted?
Is there an organizational function that is responsible for establishing the policies and auditing them to ensure compliance?  Where does that business unit fit within the organizational hierarchy?
Is there someone in the company with the official title of Head of Information Security or Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)?
What are the regulations in your industry with which you are most concerned?  For example,GDPR or Sarbanes Oxley?
Is there a formal privacy policy that defines data privacy, access control, and auditing requirements specifically for data in the analytics ecosystem?

Does the privacy policy incorporate all standard privacy principles including: Accountability, Notice, Consent, Collection Limitation, Use Limitation, Disclosure, Access and Correction, Data Accuracy, Enforcement, and Openness?
Are there documented information security policies that govern data collection, storage, transmission, retention, and destruction?

Does your analytic ecosystem  contain PII, such as Social Security Numbers (SSN); Private Health Information (PHI); customer financial records (such as bank account details); credit card numbers (PAN), or other Non-Public Information (NPI)?  Are there procedures and techniques in place to mask or obfuscated this data?

Does the company have assigned data owners for all information assets who are actively involved in setting access policy, authorizing all access to their data, and regularly reviewing who has access to data in the analytic ecosystem?

Are the data owners aware of everyone who has access to their data and where all copies of their data exist?  For example, is data copied to spreadsheets and Access databases?  If so, are the same controls applied to this data?
Are data contained in the anlaytics ecosystem classified or identified according to a standard Data Classification scheme?
Does the company apply the principle of  least privilege when granting access to sensitive data?

Does the company use role-based access controls (RBAC) within the analytics ecosystem?  Are they leveraging organizational roles across the organization, or are they unique to the Teradata data warehouse?
Are they aware of all regulatory compliance requirements resulting from the types of data in the  EDW and the jurisdictions in which they operate?
Have they ever conducted a risk assessment or audit of the analytic ecosystem to determine compliance with company policy, privacy laws, and other regulatory compliance requirements?

How many users have direct ad-hoc query access to the analytic ecosystem?   Is access always granted from the access layer or do some users have access to the acquisition and integration layers (e.g., data scientists or ETL developers)?  How is that access managed across all environments – production, test, UAT, etc.?
How many external users or business partners have access to the analytic ecosystem?
Are  shared accounts used for accessing data in the analytics ecosystem that don’t provide accountability back to the originating end user?
Is there any logging of access to sensitive data?
Is there any process in place to monitor or review access log data?
Does the company use a formal or recognized information security management system (ISMS) framework, such as ISO 2700x, as a reference or benchmark for implemented security controls within the EDW?
Does the EDW support business-critical applications where system availability is important?
Are there any known risks regarding access to sensitive data that are not being adequately managed or mitigated?
Information Category - Data Quality
How would you describe the overall quality of your data?  How does your organization handle data quality issues?  How are those issues identified and who is responsible for their resolution?
Are data quality feedback loops in place to report quality issues identifyied in the analytics ecosystem back to the operational system that is responsible for the creation of the bad data?
Is data quality measured and reported to the analytics ecosystem users at least daily so that they know if the data is of sufficient quality each day to support the analytics they plan to execute?
Is the data quality in the analytics ecosystem reported to senior management if it exceeds specified thresholds?
Are integration issues (where master data from one system doesn't not full match another) reported for resolution to a responsible person?
Information Category - Data Coverage
How much of your business leverages data for analytics today?
Is data available outside of functional applications?  (In other words, can business users access and explore data directly from an analytic ecosystem platform)
Are there business areas where there are gaps in data availability?
Is some data stored in multiple repositories (data marts, data warehouses, etc.)?
Is data integrated across the organisation into a consistent coherent scheme?
What level of historical detail is retained online?
Are prior periods summarised and retained online for analysis?
Do users frequently have to extract data from the analytics system(s) to merge it with other data that is not available on the analytics platform(s)
Application Section
Applications Section - Summary Questions
Does the business know which applications and tools to use to achieve the desired business analytics outcome? Are all desired business analytics outcomes supported by some form of technology?

When considering the analytics to address a business problem or use case, how do you know what data, or application to use? Are there different environments available for business users vs. I.T.?  Do Data Scientists have access to different analytic environments?
Are the business able to drive their business analytics outcomes with minimal assistance or do they require significant skilled support to achieve the business analytics outcome?
Is the role of each analytics application well understood and clearly differentiated to other analytics applications, or is there substantial functional or data overlap?

When considering analytics or advanced analytics, are you required to complete the analysis leveraging a specific application?  What happens if you have analytic needs that cross technologies or capabilities?
Who is responsible for application choices, IT or the Business, or a combination of both?
Do you have a data integration strategy?  How was it developed?  Are you able to extend it as new and varying data types are required (e.g., big data)?
Applications Section - Strategy

Do you have a Technology Strategy defined that supports the provisioning of technology to deliver the desired business analytics outcomes? Does this strategy address short term and long term business analytics outcomes?
Applications Section - Roadmap
Do you have a Technology Roadmap defined that supports the desired business analytics outcomes? Does this Technology Roadmap address short term and long term business analytics outcomes?

When evaluating new business solutions, are there recommended system standards for the platforms, operating systems, data bases, file systems, open source usage, cloud, etc.?  How do these standards impact the decision to move forward with a new business solution?
Applications Section - Architecture
Does your organisation view Application Architecture as a formal discipline?
Who is responsible for Application Architecture choices, I.T. or the Business, or a combination of both?
What is the decision making process to choose an application solution architecture when considering the analytics required to address a new business problem or use case. Who guides the choice?
Does your organisation have a methodical approach to designing Applications? Particularly the use of patterns that allow proven solutions to be reused wherever appropriate?

Do you have documentation (e.g. systems diagrams, descriptions, etc.) of the technology (systems, applications, tools, etc.) used to support the business? Are there similar documents for each system or major business function?
Applications Section - Data Orchestration and Processing Approach
How do business users gain access to new data?  How does this change if the data does not exist in a current system?
Do you need to know where data resides and how it is structured in order to exploit the data and perform analytics?  This is called Data Virtualisation
What types of technology support the ingestion of data into different systems?
Are there different patterns for ingesting data? I.e. What types of processes are used to ingest and transform data (e.g., traditional batch, mini-batch, trickle feed, or messaging)?
What types of technology support the integration of data for analytic use?
Are your analytics supported by common data assets such as an Event Store or Feature Store? Are they simplistic in nature or feature rich?

Describe your error reporting framework within the data integration processes.  How are decisions made about whether to reject data prior to loading or load data and follow-up on quality issues for resolution post-load?   Does it vary by analytic platform type and use case?
To what level is data lineage captured, maintained, and tracked through the analytics ecosystem?
For each type of processing, how quickly after a change in other systems is the new data loaded in the DW and available for on-line access?
Where is data latency most critical? For which data subject areas and which applications?  Where is it least critical?
Where are data latency requirements not being met? Give examples of where data latency has hindered the ability to make timely business decisions.

Which issues are causing data freshness problems (e.g., data availability windows in source systems, data volumes making processing windows exceed load windows, availability of external feeds, or transformations required between systems)?
Are there areas with business improvement opportunities if data latency is decreased?
If you have a multi-platform analytics ecosystem, how is data synchronised across platforms? How much data is duplicated across platforms in a multi-platform ecosystem
Applications Section - Analytical Applications
What type of Analytic Applications do you have in your organisation?
Are Analytic Applications used widely across your organisation?
What type of analytics are your able to perform (e.g. descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive)?
How does each user group access the data?  What kind of tools do they use, if any?  How do they learn how to use the tools?
What part of the organization determines the standards for analytic tools, programs, and technologies?  Are there different policies and standards based on the business area?
Applications Section - Availability (e.g. DR, High Availability etc.)
Does the level of availability for each analytic application meet the business need? E.g. 24 x 7, T+1
How long does it take to restore data from archive?

In the event of a disaster, do you think the systems will be available before business impact occurs. Do you know how long does it take to recover? Do you have a defined the RTO and RPO for each system?
Do you have SLA’s currently in place?  If so, what SLA’s would you say are most effective?  Are there SLA’s that may not be needed?
Are service levels and monitoring processes defined as a standard part of the project lifecycle?  How are service levels considered when transitioning an analytic from discovery to production?
How are SLA’s defined for the Analytics Ecosystem?
Are there service levels set for activities that are completed by both IT and the business?
Do service level expectations vary by time of day or shift? Do SLAs vary by business day, end of period processing, end of month, end of year etc

Are SLA’s renegotiated from time to time, based on revised, informal expectations, system improvements, or other changes?  (For example, the SLA may call for an 8:00 a.m. load completion time, but users have begun to expect completion by 6:00 a.m. based on actual completion times.)
How are analytic models monitored and updated?  Are there service levels for the review, testing, an update of analytic models used in production?
How are service level measurements collected and communicated? Are regular reports or presentations given to users and others to indicate how well service levels have been met?

What expectations from the user community are not being met regarding performance, data quality, availability, and data freshness? Are there issues that are considered a “problem” by some and “working as expected” by others?
Systems Section
Systems Section - Summary Questions
Does the business know which systems and tools to use to achieve the desired business analytics outcome? Are all desired business analytics outcomes supported by some form of technology?

When considering the analytics to address a business problem or use case, how do you know what tool or system capability to use? Are there different environments available for business users vs. I.T.?  Do Data Scientists have access to different analytic environments?
Is the role of each analytics system well understood and clearly differentiated to other analytics systems, or is there substantial functional or data overlap?
Who is responsible for technology choices, IT or the Business, or a combination of both?

Describe your approach to infrastructure support.  Are there teams dedicated to supporting platforms or specific applications?  How are the broader enterprise needs supported (such as data base, networking, data centre operations, etc.)?

Is there a single data processing and storage architecture for all analytics, or is there an ecosystem of varying processing and storage designs (including virtualisation, private cloud, public cloud and on-premise solutions) to meet a variety of analytic needs?
Systems Section - Strategy

Do you have a Technology Strategy defined that supports the provisioning of technology to deliver the desired business analytics outcomes? Does this strategy address short term and long term business analytics outcomes?
Systems Section - Roadmap
Do you have a Systems Roadmap defined that supports the desired business analytics outcomes? Does this Systems Roadmap address short term and long term business analytics outcomes?

When evaluating new business solutions, are there recommended system standards for the platforms, operating systems, data bases, file systems, open source usage, cloud, etc.?  How do these standards impact the decision to move forward with a new business solution?
Systems Section - Architecture
Does your organisation view Systems Architecture as a formal discipline?
Who is responsible for Systems Architecture choices, I.T. or the Business, or a combination of both?
Does the Systems Architecture take into consideration emerging choices and technologies (e.g. Cloud, Open Source, Big Data) to allow the architecture to evolve over time?
What is the decision making process to choose a solution architecture when considering the analytics required to address a new business problem or use case. Who guides the choice?
Does your organisation have a methodical approach to designing solutions? Particularly the use of patterns that allow proven solutions to be reused wherever appropriate?

Is there a centralized analytics ecosystem or analytics platform?  Describe the organizations responsible.  Who supports the projects that leverage each?  How is the business involved and what roles does IT play (i.e. systems administration, capacity planning, programming, etc.)

Do you have documentation (e.g. systems diagrams, descriptions, etc.) of the technology (systems, applications, tools, etc.) used to support the business? Are there similar documents for each system or major business function?
Systems Section - Storage
Does your organisation use a variety of different data storage options?
Does each system have sufficient storage for the data you want to retain? Do you know what the capacity of each type of data storage is and how much can it scale in terms of storage?
Systems Section - Infrastructure Model
Are you systems on premise, off-premise, private or public cloud?
Do security concerns limit your ability to use cloud?
Do  you utilise commodity hardware with/without system virtualisation?
Systems Section - Systems Management
Are there groups outside of IT who provide infrastructure support (networks, phones, etc.)?
How easily can new infrastructure be deployed?
Systems Section - Operations Management
Is systems operations proactive or reactive?
How are software versions kept up to date? Is this done as a regular operational activity or do software version lag behind the market? If they lag, how far do they lag?
Describe the process to update an application or put a new application into production?

Is the division of support expectations clear between the different support teams who contribute to the overall analytic output?  (This would include teams responsible for data ingest, application support, etc.) Are these expectations formalized in an Operational Level Agreement (OLA) or other document?

How are users informed about service level violations? Are alerts built into the systems?  When there are issues, who are responsible for resolution? Are root cause fixes regularly implemented based on service level violations?
Have escalation procedures been implemented for the data warehouse or analytic platform responsible for running the analytics?  Who helped  develop them?
Does your operations team have automated work tools and monitoring processes to pro-actively identify performance, data quality or user issues before trouble tickets are raised?
Does your operations team undertake proactive performance tuning and monitoring activities on a regular basis?
Do you retain enough log files or similar data to be able to detect performance, data quality or user deviations from past behaviour?
Do you have appropriate incident (ticketing) mgmt systems to be able to effectively record issues and trace them through resolution?
Do you have effective Backup and Recovery tools and processes and are these tested on a regular basis?

Does the Analytics environment operations team have standard process documents (run book, daily,  weekly , recurring and ad hoc tasks lists, communication protocols, SLA definitions, reporting requirements, etc.)
Does the team provide regular performance reports to the users, covering application and systems SLA as well as ticket processing times?
Does the Operations Team review  incoming changes and update standard documentation (e.g. runbooks, data dictionaries, system architecture diagrams etc) with the incoming changes?
Is there a prioritization system agreed with the users in place for all incoming tickets?
Are changes to the analytics environment performance-tested before being deployed into operations?
Does the Analytics environment operations team undertake regular capacity reviews to pre-empt future performance or capacity issues?
Does the Analytics environment operations team submit regular queries of different types ("Canary Queries") to test and monitor user-perceived performance?
Does the Analytics enviroment operations team undertake regular reviews of statistics collected for database performance optimization purposes?
Where workload management tools exist, does the Analytics environment operations team regularly review the workload rules to ensure that peformance is optimised
Systems Section - Teradata Platform
Do you have discreet systems and/or VM for DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD?  What is the process for promotion?
Are the system images multitenancy?
Is there any resource contention in the lower lanes (DEV, SIT, or UAT)?
Is there a formal Change Control Process for code promotion from UAT to PROD?  Does it also include instruction for backing out a change should it fail?
Do you have an automated tool to manage Data Models, Build DDL, and create automated scripts to migrate to new versions
Do you have an automated deployment process to apply the new DDL and preserve data so that DDL versions can be tracked and audited?
What layers do you have for Landing Zones, Access Layers, 1to1 views, Security Views, etc?
Are there any data restrictions?  Data with sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable content might have additional security requirements.
Do you have automated scripts to generate views?  Are they table driven?
What other processes have you developed or implemented to manage DDL or other Teradata processes
Do you have automated performance monitoring tools to watch for runaway queries, etc?
What is the process for loading data into the environments?
Do you use continuous integration software for managing automated builds?  If so, what is it?
Do developers have access to PROD?
Regarding the version control system, do you uniquely identify code release by project and environment  For example, for project Widget, you have a Widget-Dev, Widget-SIT,…,etc, for each environment?
Do you have any automated testing software or scripts?
What issues do you see most often?  For example, configuration changes, break-fix incidents, code deployments, or maintenance.
What processes are used to track these efforts?  Are there any formal process for managing requests?
Are there any Ad-Hoc executions in Production?
Regarding development, what is the process used for code management?
What is the current process for moving from a development to UAT, from your POV?
How are code defects identified and managed?
Are Data Types consistent with Class Words?
Are all columns with the same name the same data type?
Are NULLable columns used appropriately?
Do TIMESTAMPS really need to have TIME or should they just be DATE?
Are all DATE columns ANSI FORMAT?
Is PRIMARY INDEX or NO PRIMARY INDEX specified or defaulted
Is data skewing monitored?

Agility Category
Agility Section - Summary Questions
Does your organisation view agility (ability to rapidly adapt to changing circumstances) as a strategic advantage or desirable corporate capability?
Do you using development automation (eg. Automated testing, automated integration, automated deployment etc.) to improve time to market for analytics?
Do the analytics staff (in both business and IT departments) have the skills and training to be able to be effective in their roles?

Does your organsation have a specific focus on analytics user engagement (e.g. training programs, communications programs, or stakeholder engagement programs) to build a productive analytics community?
Agility Section - Strategy
Does your organisation have or plan to have reaction time to change as a measurable KPI for senior executives?
Does your organisation's processes and procedures emphasise speed of reaction as a valuable competitive dimension?
Is there a corporate push (e.g. training, compensation category, corporate function or similar) to improve the speed of response to changing market situations?
Agility Section - Roadmap
Is there a published roadmap of organisational change to improve the organisation's agility?
Is progress against the roadmap published on a regular basis to all employees?
Is there a person or committee visibly accountable for improving agility?
Agility Section - Methodology
